stem: Which enzyme joins free DNA nucleotides to form a new strand during replication?

options.content: DNA polymerase
options.rationale: Correct: it catalyses phosphodiester bond formation between nucleotides.

options.content: DNA ligase
options.rationale: Ligase joins existing fragments (Okazaki fragments), not individual nucleotides along the strand.

options.content: RNA polymerase
options.rationale: RNA polymerase makes RNA in transcription.

options.content: Restriction endonuclease
options.rationale: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences.

explanation: **DNA polymerase** adds nucleotides to the 3' end of the growing strand, forming phosphodiester bonds.

stem: What does semi-conservative replication mean?

options.content: Each new DNA molecule has one original strand and one new strand
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: One new molecule is entirely original and the other entirely new
options.rationale: This is the conservative model, which was disproved.

options.content: Each strand of the new molecules is a mixture of old and new sections
options.rationale: This is the dispersive model.

options.content: Only half of the DNA in a cell is replicated in each cycle
options.rationale: All the DNA is replicated once per cycle.

explanation: In **semi-conservative** replication each daughter molecule keeps one parental strand (conserved) and gains one new strand.

stem: In which direction does DNA polymerase build a new strand?

options.content: 3' to 5', adding nucleotides to the 5' end
options.rationale: DNA polymerase cannot add to a 5' end.

options.content: 5' to 3' on one strand and 3' to 5' on the other
options.rationale: Both new strands are made 5' to 3'; the lagging strand is made in fragments.

options.content: In either direction, depending on the template
options.rationale: The direction is fixed by the enzyme's active site.

options.content: 5' to 3', adding nucleotides to the 3' end
options.rationale: Correct: the enzyme can only extend a 3' end.

explanation: New DNA is always synthesised **5' → 3'**. This is why the lagging strand is made discontinuously.

stem: Which bonds are broken when the two strands of DNA separate before replication?

options.content: Phosphodiester bonds in the sugar-phosphate backbone
options.rationale: The backbone of each template strand stays intact.

options.content: Hydrogen bonds between complementary bases
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Peptide bonds between histone proteins
options.rationale: Peptide bonds are within proteins; strand separation breaks hydrogen bonds.

options.content: Covalent bonds between bases and sugars
options.rationale: These hold the bases on each strand and are not broken.

explanation: Separating the strands breaks the **hydrogen bonds** between paired bases; each strand stays intact as a template.

stem: Why is the lagging strand made as short Okazaki fragments?

options.content: The lagging template contains more copying errors, which must be cut out in short pieces
options.rationale: Fragments arise from the direction of synthesis, not from errors.

options.content: DNA ligase can only join short pieces of DNA
options.rationale: Ligase joins fragments that already exist; it does not cause them.

options.content: DNA polymerase works only 5' to 3', which on this template is away from the replication fork
options.rationale: Correct: the enzyme must restart repeatedly as the fork opens.

options.content: The lagging template is made of RNA rather than DNA
options.rationale: Both templates are DNA.

explanation: The templates are antiparallel. On the lagging template, 5' → 3' synthesis runs **away** from the fork, so it is made in short pieces, later joined by **ligase**.
hints: The two template strands run in opposite directions.

stem: A cell is given a drug that inhibits DNA ligase but not DNA polymerase. What would be found in newly replicated DNA?

options.content: No new DNA at all on either strand
options.rationale: DNA polymerase still works, so new nucleotides are joined.

options.content: Leading strands made of separate short fragments
options.rationale: The leading strand is made continuously and does not need ligase to join fragments.

options.content: Lagging strands made of separate short fragments
options.rationale: Correct: Okazaki fragments are made but cannot be joined.

options.content: New strands containing uracil instead of thymine
options.rationale: Inhibiting ligase does not change which nucleotides are used.

explanation: Without **ligase**, Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand stay unjoined; the leading strand is still continuous.
hints: Which strand depends on ligase to become continuous?

stem: In the Meselson and Stahl experiment, bacteria grown on ¹⁵N were moved to ¹⁴N. After one generation all the DNA formed a single band of intermediate density. Which model did this result rule out?

options.content: The semi-conservative model
options.rationale: This model predicts exactly one intermediate band.

options.content: The dispersive model
options.rationale: The dispersive model also predicts one intermediate band after one generation; it was ruled out by generation 2.

options.content: Both the semi-conservative and dispersive models
options.rationale: Both of these predict a single intermediate band after one generation.

options.content: The conservative model
options.rationale: Correct: it predicts one heavy band and one light band after one generation.

explanation: Conservative replication would keep one all-¹⁵N molecule and make one all-¹⁴N molecule: **two** bands. A single hybrid band rules it out.
hints: What would each model predict after one generation?

stem: Which result after the second generation in ¹⁴N ruled out the dispersive model?

options.content: One band of intermediate density only
options.rationale: This was the result after one generation, not two.

options.content: Two bands, one intermediate and one light
options.rationale: Correct: dispersive replication would give a single band, lighter than intermediate.

options.content: One heavy band and one light band
options.rationale: This would support the conservative model.

options.content: One band halfway between intermediate and light
options.rationale: This is what the dispersive model predicts; it was not observed.

explanation: In the dispersive model every molecule would contain a share of ¹⁵N, giving **one** band that becomes steadily lighter. Two distinct bands (hybrid and light) support semi-conservative replication.
hints: Would dispersive replication ever give completely light molecules?

stem: DNA replication takes place during the S phase of interphase.
explanation: True. S stands for synthesis: DNA replicates before mitosis or meiosis.

stem: DNA polymerase forms the hydrogen bonds between the free nucleotides and the template strand.
explanation: False. Hydrogen bonds form spontaneously by complementary base pairing. DNA polymerase catalyses the **phosphodiester bonds** between adjacent nucleotides.

stem: Match each term with its role in replication.

right.content: Exposes bases to which free nucleotides pair
Raw material for the new strand
Forms phosphodiester bonds between nucleotides of the new strand

explanation: Template strands direct the sequence; nucleotides pair; polymerase builds the backbone; ligase seals fragments.

stem: Choose the correct words.

payload.template: On the {{blank:a}} strand the new DNA is made continuously, while on the {{blank:b}} strand it is made in short {{blank:c}} fragments.

explanation: Leading strand: continuous. Lagging strand: discontinuous, Okazaki fragments.

stem: Name the enzyme that joins Okazaki fragments together.
explanation: **DNA ligase** forms phosphodiester bonds between adjacent fragments.

stem: Bacteria whose DNA contains only ¹⁵N are transferred to a medium containing only ¹⁴N and allowed to divide for four generations. Assuming semi-conservative replication, what percentage of the DNA molecules contain only ¹⁴N?
explanation: After 4 generations there are 2⁴ = 16 molecules. Two contain an original ¹⁵N strand (hybrid); 14 are all-¹⁴N. 14 ÷ 16 × 100 = 87.5%. 75% is the answer after three generations.
workedSolution: 1. After 4 generations there are 2⁴ = 16 molecules. Two contain an original ¹⁵N strand (hybrid); 14 are all-¹⁴N. 14 ÷ 16 × 100 = 87.5%. 75% is the answer after three generations.
hints: The two original strands are never split up.

stem: A bacterium has a circular chromosome of $3.0 \times 10^{6}$ base pairs. Replication starts at one origin, and two replication forks move in opposite directions, each copying 750 base pairs per second. Calculate the time taken to replicate the whole chromosome, in minutes, to three significant figures.
explanation:
1. Each fork copies half the chromosome: $3.0 \times 10^{6} \div 2 = 1.5 \times 10^{6}$ base pairs.
2. Time $= 1.5 \times 10^{6} \div 750 = 2000$ s.
3. In minutes: $2000 \div 60 = 33.3$ minutes.
4. Forgetting that there are two forks doubles the answer (66.7 min); leaving it in seconds gives 2000.
workedSolution:
1. 1. Each fork copies half the chromosome: $3.0 \times 10^{6} \div 2 = 1.5 \times 10^{6}$ base pairs.
2. Time $= 1.5 \times 10^{6} \div 750 = 2000$ s.
3. In minutes: $2000 \div 60 = 33.3$ minutes.
4. Forgetting that there are two forks doubles the answer (66.7 min); leaving it in seconds gives 2000.

stem: Describe the process of semi-conservative replication of DNA.

points.description: Double helix unwinds; hydrogen bonds between bases break and the strands separate
Each strand acts as a template
Free (activated) DNA nucleotides pair with exposed bases by complementary base pairing (A-T, C-G)
DNA polymerase joins nucleotides by forming phosphodiester bonds (5' to 3')
Each new molecule has one original and one new strand; lagging strand fragments joined by ligase

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The double helix unwinds and the hydrogen bonds between the bases break, so the two strands separate. Each strand acts as a template. Free DNA nucleotides pair with the exposed bases by complementary base pairing, A with T and C with G. DNA polymerase joins the nucleotides by forming phosphodiester bonds, building each new strand in the 5' to 3' direction; on the lagging strand the fragments are joined by DNA ligase. Each new DNA molecule contains one original strand and one new strand.

explanation: Unwind, template, pair, polymerase, semi-conservative result.

stem: Explain how the results of the Meselson and Stahl experiment after one and two generations support the semi-conservative model and not the others.

points.description: Generation 1: one band of intermediate (hybrid) density
This rules out conservative replication, which predicts one heavy and one light band
Generation 2: two bands, intermediate and light, in equal amounts
This rules out dispersive replication, which predicts one band of density between hybrid and light; only semi-conservative fits both

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: After one generation in ¹⁴N all the DNA formed one intermediate band, so every molecule had one ¹⁵N strand and one ¹⁴N strand; conservative replication would have given a heavy band and a light band. After two generations there were two bands, intermediate and light, in equal amounts. Dispersive replication would have given a single band lighter than intermediate. Only semi-conservative replication predicts both results.

explanation: Generation 1 rules out conservative; generation 2 rules out dispersive.

stem: Explain why accurate DNA replication is important.

points.description: The base sequence carries the genetic code / codes for the amino acid sequence of proteins
Daughter cells need identical copies of the genes to make the correct proteins and function
Errors are mutations, which may produce faulty proteins / could lead to uncontrolled division (cancer)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The sequence of bases is the genetic code for the amino acid sequences of proteins. Each daughter cell must receive an identical copy so it can make the correct proteins. Copying errors are mutations, which can change proteins and may lead to disease or cancer.

explanation: Code → proteins → function; errors are mutations.
hints: What does the base sequence code for?

stem: Bacteria were grown for many generations in a medium with ¹⁵NH₄Cl as the only nitrogen source, then transferred to a medium containing ¹⁴NH₄Cl. DNA was extracted at intervals and centrifuged in a caesium chloride density gradient. The position of each band was recorded as heavy, intermediate or light.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Explain why nitrogen is used to label DNA.

points.description: Nitrogen is present in the bases of DNA (so heavy N makes the DNA denser)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The nitrogenous bases contain nitrogen, so ¹⁵N is built into new DNA and makes it denser.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What band pattern would the conservative model predict after one generation in ¹⁴N?

options.content: One intermediate band only
options.rationale: This is the semi-conservative (and dispersive) prediction.

options.content: One heavy band and one light band
options.rationale: Correct: the original molecule stays heavy; the new one is all light.

options.content: One light band only
options.rationale: The original heavy DNA would still be present.

options.content: One heavy band only
options.rationale: New DNA made with ¹⁴N would be light.

parts.explanation: Conservative: original molecule intact (heavy) plus an all-new molecule (light).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Assuming semi-conservative replication, what percentage of the DNA molecules would be intermediate after three generations?
parts.explanation: After 3 generations there are $2^3 = 8$ molecules; 2 are hybrid: $2/8 \times 100 = 25\%$.
parts.workedSolution: 1. After 3 generations there are $2^3 = 8$ molecules; 2 are hybrid: $2/8 \times 100 = 25\%$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Describe the band pattern expected after two generations if replication were dispersive, and explain why.

points.description: One band only, between intermediate and light (lighter than generation 1)
Every molecule would contain some old ¹⁵N DNA mixed with new ¹⁴N, in equal shares

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A single band, lighter than intermediate but heavier than light, because in dispersive replication every molecule would contain scattered pieces of old ¹⁵N DNA with new ¹⁴N DNA, with the ¹⁵N shared equally among all molecules.

explanation: Density bands distinguish the three models; semi-conservative predicts one hybrid band, then hybrid and light bands.
hints: Each model predicts a different number of bands.

stem: A short section of a DNA molecule is about to be replicated. One strand has the sequence 3' TACGGATC 5'.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Write the sequence of the new strand built on this template, from its 5' end to its 3' end (letters only).
parts.explanation: Complementary pairing: T-A, A-T, C-G, G-C, G-C, A-T, T-A, C-G gives 5' ATGCCTAG 3'.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: This new strand is made continuously. Which statement explains why?

options.content: DNA ligase joins its nucleotides as they arrive
options.rationale: Ligase joins fragments; polymerase adds single nucleotides.

options.content: The template contains no thymine
options.rationale: The template contains thymine; the base composition is irrelevant.

options.content: DNA polymerase can add nucleotides in either direction on this particular template strand
options.rationale: DNA polymerase works only 5' to 3'.

options.content: Its template is read 3' to 5' as the fork opens, so synthesis follows the fork
options.rationale: Correct: this is the leading strand.

parts.explanation: Synthesis 5' → 3' follows the opening fork on this template, so the strand is the leading strand.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State the role of DNA polymerase and of hydrogen bonding in making this new strand.

points.description: Hydrogen bonds form between complementary bases of free nucleotides and the template (spontaneously)
DNA polymerase catalyses phosphodiester bonds between adjacent nucleotides of the new strand

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Free nucleotides are held against the template by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases; DNA polymerase then joins neighbouring nucleotides by catalysing phosphodiester bonds.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: True or false: the new DNA molecule formed will contain the template strand and the new strand.

explanation: Complementary pairing determines the sequence; polymerase builds the backbone 5' → 3'.
hints: The new strand is antiparallel to the template.
